notes_in.text: DNF on touches. About 12 m back, the course turns sharply LEFT, so the trailer rear has to go left. I swung the trailer too late, and its rear-right corner kept hitting the outside rail. Retrying with small fixes from the same spot used up the touch budget. Priority: start the left swing a few metres before the bend and hold a hitch angle of about 30 degrees through it. Watch the tractor as well: with a big left hitch, its front-right corner swings into the right rail. Tip: the hitch reacts quickly, so reverse slowly and keep both sides of the rig in view.

note.text: Finished in 112 s with no touches in the S-bend. Both touches came at the end: the trailer's rear-right corner hit the dock wall because I steered toward the bay with the trailer still angled 20 to 30 degrees. The fix was to pull forward until the trailer was straight, then reverse slowly, steering only to keep the hitch at zero. The bay lines up with the final straight, so follow the rails, not the bay corners. Priority: get the trailer straight before the last few metres. Tip: the trailer reacts fast, so reverse slowly and keep the hitch under 35 degrees.

notes_in.text: Finished but touched the left rail 5 times. The alley seems to bend near the end, and steering by the gap between the rails let the cart drift left. The bay sits right of the alley centre, so watch its painted corners early. The short cart reacts fast: keep hitch targets small, steer gently and reverse at about 0.3 m/s. Pull-forwards caused touches because the mower's nose swings into the rail, so avoid them, or keep them short and straight. Tip: if the front is pinned, reverse with the wheels turned slightly toward that rail. The nose swings off and the cart still goes in straight.

DNF on touches. The alley bends right about halfway. My cart drifted onto the left (outer) rail before the bend. Every rescue after that was a short forward-and-reverse shunt, and the mower's left corners kept hitting that rail, front-left most often. Priority: keep the whole rig in the inside (right) half before the bend, and start turning the cart right early and gently. Watch all four mower corners as well as the cart. Tip: this cart is very short, so its hitch angle changes fast. Reverse slowly and stop well before a rail, not just before contact.

The alley bends right partway down, and the bay sits near the right rail. I lost time steering at the bay, or at the gap I could see between the rails: the cart cut the corner and the mower's front swung into the rails, which caused 6 touches. What worked was mapping the walls once, then pulling forward about 2 m to line up with the approach alley. After that, reverse slowly so the cart's rear follows a planned line: straight, round the bend, then along the bay. Keep the hitch under about 30 degrees. Tip: this short cart folds fast, so reverse at about 0.3 m/s.

note.text: Finished in 59 s with no touches. What worked: keep a running map of every rail point you see, with your head turned fully back, and steer the cart along the widest clear opening, not the midpoint between the rails. At the bend the right rail drops out of view, and the midpoint then pulls you onto the outer rail. Once the bay is in sight, aim the cart's rear at its centre and straighten before you arrive. Reverse at about 0.3 m/s. Tip: the hitch overshot when the bend started, so keep hitch targets small and steer firmly. It recovers without pulling forward.

This course turns RIGHT going backwards. I lost time early: the trailer's rear-left corner hit the left rail four times because I reversed straight or let a gap-seeking steer pull the trailer left. What worked: pull forward on left lock until the car points slightly left in the lane, then reverse at walking pace holding the trailer swung right about 20 degrees through the bend, watching the reversing camera. Once the painted bay corners show, track the bay centre line and straighten gradually; the leg ends once lined up. Commit to the turn early; shuffling costs most.

Finished in 65 s with one touch. My first controller aimed the trailer the wrong way. To send the trailer's rear left you need a negative hitch angle, not a positive one. Hitch hit 48 deg, I pulled forward and clipped the front-left corner on a rail. Once fixed, gap-seeking from the camera with dead-reckoned rail memory took the L-turn smoothly at about 1 m/s. I reached the bay 16 deg skewed. A short straight pull forward of about 3 m, then a slow reverse holding the hitch near zero, parked it. Tip: this short box trailer folds fast, so go slow and pull forward before the hitch reaches 40 deg.
